verdict.rationale: Link CLI documents per-purchase consent before money moves: the agent creates a spend request, "Customers approve each request on the Link website or in the mobile app," and only then receives a one-time-use credential. SPTs act as scoped mandates with max_amount, currency, expiry and revocation. The MCP server separately requires human confirmation, via an approval token that expires after 24h, before outbound payments and refunds. The community note that MPP itself has no authorization layer marks a gap on that rail; it does not contradict Link's approval flow. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the approval step, and a documented human-consent gate for MPP/x402 machine payments and the ACS embedded checkout flow.
